sections.s-hero: Welcome. Let me start with the question this course exists to answer: what do you do when you are ready to grow, but you love it here? For a long time, the honest answer was to look somewhere else, and Vanderbilt lost good people that way. The Talent Marketplace changes that. It is Vanderbilt's home for your growth and development: a place to explore what you could become, build the skills to get there, and be ready when the opportunity arises, all without leaving the university. Over the next fifteen minutes I will show you what the marketplace is, the different ways people enter it, how a move actually happens from everyday growth to a planned handoff, and the promises that make the whole thing safe. Stay at Vanderbilt. Go somewhere new.
sections.s-charge: You might wonder why a course about your career starts with the university's strategy. Here is why: they are the same story. Vanderbilt's charge is bold: define the great university of the twenty-first century, and be it. Look at what that actually takes. Exceptional core operations means thousands of people doing skilled work, better every year. Bold strategic initiatives need people who can step into brand-new problems. Values leadership needs people who stay long enough to carry the culture. A university can buy that talent from the outside, slowly and at high cost, or it can grow its own and keep it. That second path is the marketplace, and it is why your growth is not a side benefit here; it is the strategy. Dare to grow.
sections.s-what: So what is the Talent Marketplace? The easiest way to understand it is to picture two colleagues. The first is an analyst who dreams of project management. She names it as a career of interest, the marketplace shows her the skills the role takes, and she starts closing the gap with learning tied to that goal. When a role opens, staff like her see it before the public does. That is the long game: careers of interest. The second colleague loves his job, but another unit is running a project he would learn a lot from. With his manager's OK he joins it for a defined stretch, keeps his home job the whole time, and comes back with new skills and new relationships. That is the short game: short projects in other units. Two paths, one marketplace, both in Oracle. And notice what protected both of them: nothing they explored alerted anyone, and leaders only ever see group totals. When you are ready, test yourself with fact or fiction; most people are surprised by at least one answer.
sections.s-entrances: People arrive at the marketplace from very different places, so let me show you the three kinds of talent it serves. Maybe you are fifteen years in with excellent reviews, and the work runs on autopilot; you love your team, you just miss being stretched. You are looking to grow. Or maybe you were hired as a financial analyst and quietly became your unit's data visualization expert, doing valuable work your job description never mentions. You are hidden talent, and the marketplace is how the university finally sees you. Or maybe your division just merged, half your duties moved, and the role you signed up for no longer exists; you still believe in this place, you just need the right seat. You are not in the right fit, but you are right for the mission. Six doors cover these three situations, and every one of them opens the same way: a growth conversation with your manager. Open each door, walk the path inside, and find the one closest to where you are today.
sections.s-process: Now let me walk you through how a move actually happens, because it is simpler than most people fear. The process has two beats. The first beat is every day, and nothing about it is an application. You keep your skills honest and current. You flag the careers that interest you. You take learning tied to your goals. All of it stays private, and all of it is just growing. The second beat begins when an opening appears. Staff see eligible openings before the public does, so you get the first look. You apply, you interview like any other candidate, and if you are chosen, the managers and HR plan the handoff together, so your old team is never left stranded. Here is the insight to keep: the person who wins the role is almost always the one who used the everyday beat to get ready. Growth is daily; readiness is the reward. Try calling the next move to see the whole sequence play out.
sections.s-culture: Now the part that decides whether everything I just described actually works: the culture. Imagine telling your manager you are a serious candidate for a role in another unit. What happens in the next thirty seconds shapes your whole career here. The research is sobering: about three out of four managers admit to holding on to strong team members. Not from malice; from real pressure to deliver with the team they have. But that grip quietly stops people from moving inside, and the people who cannot move inside eventually move outside. So Vanderbilt made the promises plain. No retaliation, ever. No watching who explores. And managers coach. Listen to the model response: thank you for telling me. What drew you to it? How can I help you prepare well? Hear the difference? One sentence of gratitude turns a resignation risk into a development plan. And for the manager, releasing talent is a win on the record: the university keeps the skills, and a reputation for growing people attracts the next strong hire. Take the five manager responses and decide which build this culture and which break it.
sections.s-plan: Everything you have learned now becomes five small moves, and each one exists for a reason. Move one: have a growth conversation with your manager, because every path in the marketplace starts with that talk. Move two: build your plan in the Talent Marketplace tool, so where I am and where I want to go stops being a feeling and becomes something you can see. Move three: update your career preferences in Oracle, because the matching can only work with what you tell it. Move four: level your skills honestly, both the skills you have and the ones you are developing; padded ratings get found out in interviews, honest ones compound. Move five: flag your careers of interest in Grow, privately, so opportunity can start finding you. Every link opens the real screen in Oracle, and the printable job aid carries all five moves with you. One move today is enough, and the best first move is the conversation.
sections.s-recap: Before we close, let us find out what stuck. Six questions, and every one is a situation you could actually meet this year: what your manager sees the moment you declare an interest, what a short project really earns you, when outside candidates can enter the race. Answer honestly, and read the why after each answer; that is where the learning lives. Most people are surprised by at least one. See how you do.
sections.s-close: You came in with a question: how do I grow without leaving? Now you have the answer, and it fits in one breath. The Talent Marketplace is Vanderbilt's home for your growth and development. Identify where you want to grow. Build the skills, with your manager's support, a little every day. And when the opportunity arises, pursue it, ready. Your activity stays private until you act, and the promises protect you the whole way. So here is your one next step, and it is already on your list: a conversation with your manager about your growth and development. Put it on the calendar this week. Thank you for spending fifteen minutes on your future here. Now go grow.
